purpose:
A TWO-STEP form whose submit is refused SILENTLY: the validator writes the refusal into step 1's plain

message node — hidden while step 2 is shown — and changes nothing visible on the page the commit was clicked on. The message lives where the FIELD lives (step 1 owns Phone Number and its message node); the review step owns 'Submit Application' and no message node at all. This is the summit-life-carrier failure wearing vkpower's markup: no ARIA role, no aria-invalid, no error id convention — nothing the anchored attribution ladder can read, so only the step-back walk plus the forward-pass text snapshot can name the refusal.
targeted_defect: Regression guard for B1-S (the step-back rejection reader) and its forward-walk text licence: a crawler that only reads the page it crossed from records outcome=none with zero rejections named, which is the most misleading bundle shape there is. Also guards the B2 closed loop's live shape: the refusal names its field and draws its mask, so one evidence-driven re-fill and one retry must complete the journey.
lane_note: The behaviour under test is a real step transition driven by input events (Continue enables only once both fields hold text), visibility-scoped capture of display:none regions, and a live submit handler writing into a hidden node — exactly the rendered-layout semantics (getBoundingClientRect-based visibility) jsdom does not implement, so the jsdom lane cannot adjudicate this fixture.

hidden_step_is_invisible.why: The Submit Application button and step 2's texts are display:none on load; the inventory's own visibility rule must exclude them, because that same rule is what makes the hidden message node unreadable from step 2 — the phenomenon under test, not a special case.
